paragraphs.source_en: Puzzled, Kyūhachirō asked, “Why is that white banner in the hands of one of your men?”

paragraphs.source_en: “I picked it up on the road.”

units.source_en: “I picked it up on the road.”

paragraphs.source_en: “You picked up a treasured banner handed down through generations—from the road?”

units.source_en: “You picked up a treasured banner handed down through generations—from the road?”

paragraphs.source_en: “Indeed. When I picked it up, Okinpei beside me even called out to the enemy standard-bearer—Katsuyori, Katsuyori! You may be fleeing for your life in disgrace, but surely that is no reason to surrender your ancestral treasure banner to the enemy! What a disgrace!”

units.source_en: “Indeed. When I picked it up, Okinpei beside me even called out to the enemy standard-bearer—Katsuyori, Katsuyori! You may be fleeing for your life in disgrace, but surely that is no reason to surrender your ancestral treasure banner to the enemy!
units.source_zh: “是啊，我捡起来的时候，旁边的尾金平还对敌人的旗手说呢——胜赖呀胜赖，虽说你现在正在狼狈逃命，可也不至于把先祖传下来的宝旗交给敌人啊！

units.source_en: What a disgrace!”

paragraphs.source_zh: “是啊，我捡起来的时候，旁边的尾金平还对敌人的旗手说呢——胜赖呀胜赖，虽说你现在正在狼狈逃命，可也不至于把先祖传下来的宝旗交给敌人啊！成何体统！”

units.source_en: “Was his plight truly so wretched?”
units.source_zh: “有这么狼狈吗？”

paragraphs.source_en: Kyūhachirō did not laugh; instead, he sighed. The victor becomes a king and the vanquished an outlaw; some invisible force in this world was mercilessly passing judgment on all things. This victory filled him with desolation, and he lamented humanity’s cruelty: “I wonder with what face the renowned Katsuyori can return to Kai. His army of fifteen thousand has been almost completely destroyed.”

paragraphs.source_en: “Do not dwell on it. If he returns to Shinano, Kōsaka Danjō alone has more than eight thousand soldiers waiting for him at Kaizu.”

units.source_en: “Do not dwell on it. If he returns to Shinano, Kōsaka Danjō alone has more than eight thousand soldiers waiting for him at Kaizu.”
units.source_zh: “别想那么多，如果他回到信州，光是海津的高坂弹正就有八千多士兵在等着他呢。”

paragraphs.source_en: The war had been won, yet he felt lonely—why was that? Kyūhachirō reproached himself. If he grieved for his retainers who had died, then the sorrow of Katsuyori, who had lost fifteen thousand men, was surely beyond the power of the brush to describe.

paragraphs.source_en: Did the glittering stars look the same to Katsuyori as he fled in disarray as they did to Nobunaga and Ieyasu? Were they equally enchanting to them all? For some reason, strange thoughts like these kept coming to Kyūhachirō.
